references.text: Moses emphasizes that he cannot act on his own authority, but only according to God's command, paralleling Jesus' statement that he can do nothing of himself.
The prophet describes a servant who listens to God's word to judge righteously, just as Jesus says that he judges as he hears.
The Lord emphasizes that he acts not on his own initiative, but according to God's will, which reflects Jesus' claim that he does not seek his own will.
Jesus repeats the theme that he does not act on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing, and that he always does what pleases him.
Jesus confirms that he has come to do the Father's will, not his own, as a direct response to the question about his authority.
Jesus explains that his teaching is not his own, but from the one who sent him, and that whoever seeks their own glory is deceitful, unlike the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him.
